name: The Beacon Spire
lesson: C2 beaconing and DNS anomalies: regular check-ins with fixed sizes, encoded identifiers in URLs, and long encoded subdomains in TXT lookups.
pivot_tip: Pivot on src and regularity. Humans browse in bursts; implants check in every N seconds with the same byte count.
reaction: The HTTPS beacon went silent and the DNS lookups doubled. VELVET LOCUST switched channels.

e701.title: Proxy: VAULT-DB-01 outbound
lines: VAULT-DB-01 (10.20.9.50) outbound web requests, last 2 hours:
stat-sync.example  203.0.113.66  every ~300 s (+/- 20 s)  bytes_out=512  bytes_in=128
No other destinations. Database servers have no business browsing the web.
e701.tip: A tight interval histogram plus identical sizes is a heartbeat. Jitter of a few percent is designed to look random; it rarely does.

e702.title: Resolver stats: TXT lookups by host
lines: VAULT-DB-01  31   all to *.t.cdn-metrics.test, 24-char hex labels, unique every time
Average query name length: MAIL-GW-01 26 chars, VAULT-DB-01 45 chars
e702.tip: Long, unique, encoded-looking subdomains in TXT lookups from a server are a DNS tunnel. The data rides in the name and the answer.

e703.title: svchelper.exe config (from triage memory)
e703.tip: Configs tell you the adversary's backup plan. Block every channel at once, or they fail over. Note seal_key: you'll need it later.

e704.title: VAULT-DB-01 business profile
lines: Role        : Ledger database for Halcyon Dynamics (crown jewels)
Owner       : Finance Systems   RTO: 4 hours   Data: 7 years of ledger + payroll
Approved egress: payroll-suite.example (192.0.2.90) over HTTPS ONLY
Isolation   : allowed only with CFO sign-off (obtained 10:50 for incident response)
e704.tip: Know the asset: its one approved destination makes everything else stand out, and the sign-off means you can contain it.

objectives.title: Check the proxy
hints: The Web Proxy node.
Press E at PROXY-01.
Open 'Proxy: VAULT-DB-01 outbound'.

objectives.title: Find the heartbeat
objectives.desc: Hunt the proxy table for the C2 domain you first saw in the Execution Fields. Then try '| count by src'.
objectives.success: Twenty check-ins, five minutes apart, all from 10.20.9.50. The vault is beaconing.
hints: Remember updchk.exe's check-in domain from Zone 2?
It was stat-sync.example.
search proxy where domain="stat-sync.example"

objectives.title: Who's calling home?
objectives.desc: The beacon URI carries an encoded id. Decode it: decode base64 b7-001
objectives.success: VAULT-DB-01;svchelper;v2.4. The implant from the Bridges, now on the vault.
hints: The id= value in the URI is Base64.
decode can take a row id.
decode base64 b7-001

objectives.title: Read the rhythm
objectives.prompt: Requests every ~300 s (+/- 20 s), always 512 bytes out and 128 bytes in, from a database server. What does that pattern mean?

options.feedback: People browse in bursts with varying sizes, and nobody browses from a database server.

options.text: Automated C2 beaconing: an implant checking in on a timer with small jitter

options.feedback: 128 bytes in per request is a heartbeat, not a download.
Updates go to updates.osvendor.example, not a look-alike domain, and pull megabytes.

objectives.success: Right. Regular interval, fixed size, odd source: a beacon.
hints: Look at regularity and size.
Software, not people, does things exactly every five minutes.
The beaconing option.

objectives.title: The second channel
objectives.desc: Hunt the dns table for TXT lookups from VAULT-DB-01. (Try '| count by host' on all TXT lookups first.)
objectives.solution: search dns where qtype="TXT" and host="VAULT-DB-01"
objectives.success: 31 TXT lookups with random-looking hex labels under t.cdn-metrics.test. A DNS tunnel.
hints: Mail servers do TXT lookups for SPF. Who else does?
Filter qtype and host.
search dns where qtype="TXT" and host="VAULT-DB-01"

objectives.title: What rides in the tunnel?
objectives.desc: One TXT answer is longer than the rest. Decode it: decode hex d-700
objectives.success: They're staging ledger_q3.7z in 412 chunks. The crown jewels are being packed.
hints: The answer field of d-700 is hex.
decode hex works on row ids too.
decode hex d-700

objectives.title: Know the enemy's plan B
objectives.desc: Collect the resolver stats, the implant config, and the vault's business profile.
hints: DNS-RES-01, FORENSICS-LAB, VAULT-DB-01.
Press E at each.
Open all three records.

objectives.title: Form a hypothesis
objectives.desc: Press B. Pin the proof and choose.
objectives.prompt: How is VELVET LOCUST controlling the vault?

options.text: svchelper.exe beacons over HTTPS to stat-sync.example, with a DNS TXT tunnel (and an emergency domain) as fallback

options.feedback: The RDP session ended at 10:31. The beacons continue without it.
MAIL-GW-01's TXT lookups are SPF/DMARC checks. Compare the query names.
payroll-suite.example is the approved destination. The beacons go elsewhere.

objectives.success: Confirmed: application-layer C2 over web and DNS.
hints: Pin the proxy record and the resolver stats.
Count the channels in the config.
Pin e701 and e702, then choose the HTTPS + DNS option.

objectives.title: Map it to ATT&CK
objectives.desc: Press M and map both channels.
hints: Both are ways to talk to the controller.
Command and Control: Application Layer Protocol.
f1 -> T1071.001 Web Protocols; f2 -> T1071.004 DNS.

objectives.title: Cut every channel at once
objectives.desc: Press R. Preserve, then block primary, fallback, and emergency together.
hints: Blocking one channel makes them fail over to the next.
Memory first, then all three channels in one change, then lock down the vault's egress.
Memory, block all C2 channels together, restrict egress, add beacon detection.

f1.text: svchelper.exe beacons every ~300 s over HTTPS to stat-sync.example
f1.hint: Command and control hiding in ordinary web traffic.

f2.text: TXT lookups with encoded labels under t.cdn-metrics.test carry C2 data
f2.hint: Command and control hiding in DNS.

responses.label: Capture memory on VAULT-DB-01
responses.description: Full RAM image of the vault before blocking.
responses.tradeoff: Five minutes. Preserves the staging state.
responses.feedback: Memory captured. The staging folder and chunk list are preserved.

responses.label: Block ALL channels together: stat-sync.example, *.cdn-metrics.test, edge-relay.test, 203.0.113.66, 198.51.100.77
responses.description: Proxy block + internal DNS sinkhole + egress firewall in one change.
responses.tradeoff: One coordinated change. No fallback left.
responses.too_early: Grab memory first. Once the C2 drops, the implant may wipe its staging state.
responses.feedback: All three channels dead at once. The implant is talking to a sinkhole.

responses.label: Restrict VAULT-DB-01 egress to payroll-suite.example only
responses.feedback: The vault can now only reach the payroll vendor.

responses.label: Deploy beacon and DNS-tunnel detections
responses.description: Alert on periodic outbound connections and long unique TXT labels.
responses.tradeoff: Needs some tuning for monitoring tools.

responses.label: Block stat-sync.example now; deal with DNS later
responses.feedback: The implant failed over to DNS within a minute, and the staging sped up. Block every channel in one move.

responses.label: Block all DNS TXT lookups company-wide
responses.description: Drop every TXT query at the resolver.
responses.tradeoff: Mail authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) depends on TXT records.
responses.feedback: The mail gateway can't check SPF or DMARC anymore and is quarantining good mail. Block the bad domains, not the record type.
